He played [[college basketball]] for the [[University of Memphis]], where he played four years for the [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Tigers basketball team]]. ==College career== Stephens was not a highly regarded recruit out of Harker Heights High School when he was offered a scholarship by Memphis coach [[Josh Pastner]]. By his senior year at Memphis, however, he had become a crowd favorite for his spectacular dunking and blocking abilities. In 2011–12, he won the Intersport's Dunks of the Year title for a dunk against Xavier on February 4, 2012.{{cite web|url=http://www.gotigersgo.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/stephens_dj00.html |title=30 D.J. Stephens |work=GoTigersGo.com |access-date=March 15, 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150217214636/http://www.gotigersgo.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/stephens_dj00.html |archive-date=February 17, 2015 }} In his senior year at Memphis, Stephens became a starter and earned the Conference USA defensive player of the year award. Stephens earned national attention in the 2013 NCAA tournament after demonstrating his leaping ability against St. Mary's and Michigan State. In a four-year career at Memphis, Stephens played a total of 129 games while averaging 4.0 points, 3.4 rebounds and 1.2 blocks in 13.2 minutes per game.{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/dj-stephens-1.html|title=D.J. Stephens Stats|work=Sports-Reference.com|access-date=October 23, 2015}} ==Professional career== ===Ilysiakos (2013–2014)=== During the 2013 pre-draft workouts at the [[NBA Draft Combine]], Stephens recorded the highest standing vertical leap (46 inches) and the highest running vertical leap (53 inches) ever recorded by the NBA.{{cite web|last=Busbee |first=Jay |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/blogs/nba-ball-dont-lie/nba-draft-dj-stephens-records-highest-vertical-leap-181932411.html |title=NBA Draft: DJ Stephens records the highest vertical leap ever measured by the NBA |work=Yahoo.com |date=March 23, 2013 |access-date=March 15, 2014}} He also had the fastest time at the 2013 Combine in the three-quarter court sprint.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/140512-combine-primer|title=A Closer Look at the Draft Combine|access-date=May 12, 2014|date=May 12, 2014|work=NBA.com}} After going undrafted in the [[2013 NBA draft]], Stephens joined the Miami Heat for the Orlando Summer League and the Dallas Mavericks for the Las Vegas Summer League after his shot step in Masaje Arisco. On August 13, 2013, he signed with [[Ilysiakos B.C.]] of [[Greek Basketball League|Greece]] for the 2013–14 season.{{cite news|title=Ilysiakos signs rookie DJ Stephens|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/greece/104938/ilysiakos-signs-rookie-dj-stephens.html|access-date=December 2, 2014|work=Sportando.com|date=August 13, 2013}} In early March 2014, he left Greece and returned to the United States.{{cite news|title=DJ Stephens reportedly leaving Ilysiakos to sign in the NBA|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/usa/nba/113795/dj-stephens-reportedly-leaving-ilysiakos-to-sign-in-the-nba.html|access-date=December 2, 2014|work=Sportando.com|date=March 14, 2014}} ===Milwaukee Bucks (2014)=== On March 26, 2014, Stephens signed a 10-day contract with the Milwaukee Bucks.{{cite news|title=Bucks Sign Free-Agent Guard/Forward D.J. Stephens|url=http://www.nba.com/bucks/release/bucks-sign-free-agent-guardforward-dj-stephens|access-date=December 2, 2014|work=NBA.com|date=March 26, 2014}} On March 29, 2014, he made his NBA debut. In just under 12 minutes of action, he recorded five points and four rebounds in a loss to the Miami Heat.{{cite news|title=Notebook: Heat 88, Bucks 67|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20140329/MIAMIL/gameinfo.html|access-date=December 2, 2014|work=NBA.com|date=March 29, 2014}} On April 5, 2014, the Bucks did not offer him a second 10-day contract after his first 10-day contract expired.{{cite news|title=Bucks Won't Sign D.J. Stephens To 2nd 10-Day Contract|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/232782/Bucks-Wont-Sign-DJ-Stephens-To-2nd-10-Day-Contract|access-date=December 2, 2014|work=realgm.com|date=April 5, 2014}} ===Anadolu Efes (2014)=== On April 10, 2014, he signed with [[Anadolu Efes S.K.|Anadolu Efes]] of Turkey for the rest of the 2013–14 season.{{cite news|title=DJ Stephens lands in Istanbul to join Anadolu Efes|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/turkey/116750/dj-stephens-lands-in-istanbul-to-join-anadolu-efes.html|access-date=April 11, 2014|work=Sportando.com|date=April 10, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140413140627/http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/turkey/116750/dj-stephens-lands-in-istanbul-to-join-anadolu-efes.html|archive-date=April 13, 2014|url-status=dead}} ===Zenit Saint Petersburg (2014–2015)=== On October 1, 2014, Stephens signed with the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].{{cite news|title=Pelicans Add D.J. Stephens to Training Camp Roster|url=http://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-add-d.j.-stephens-training-camp-roster|access-date=December 2, 2014|work=NBA.com|date=October 1, 2014}} However, he was later waived by the Pelicans on October 24, 2014.{{cite news|title=Pelicans Request Waivers on Jones and Stephens|url=http://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-request-waivers-jones-and-stephens|access-date=December 2, 2014|work=NBA.com|date=October 24, 2014}} On December 2, 2014, he signed with [[B.C. Zenit Saint Petersburg|Zenit Saint Petersburg]] of Russia for the rest of the season.{{cite news|title=Zenit St. Petersburg announces DJ Stephens|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/russia/143305/zenit-st-petersburg-announces-dj-stephens.html|access-date=December 2, 2014|work=Sportando.com|date=December 2, 2014}} In 21 league games Stephens|work=OurSportsCentral.com|date=March 5, 2016|access-date=March 5, 2016}} ===Iowa Energy (2016)=== On March 5, 2016, Stephens was traded to the [[Iowa Energy]] in exchange for a 2016 fifth-round draft pick. The next day, he made his debut for Iowa in a 109–104 loss to the [[Delaware 87ers]], recording three points and four rebounds in 17 minutes off the bench.{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/games/20160306/DELIWA/|title=Smith Scores 50 To Spark 87ers|work=NBA.com|date=March 6, 2016|access-date=March 6, 2016}} On March 28, he was named NBA Development League Performer of the Week after averaging 24.7 points on 61.4 percent shooting to go with 8.0 rebounds, 2.0 blocks, 1.3 assists and 1.3 steals while connecting 11-of-18 three-point attempts in three games from March 21 through March 27.{{cite web|url=http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/iowas-d-j-stephens-named-nba-development-league-performer-of-the-week/n-5116138|title=Iowa's D.J. Stephens Named NBA Development League Performer of the Week|work=OurSportsCentral.com|date=March 28, 2016|access-date=March 28, 2016}} ===Budivelnyk (2016–2017)=== In July 2016, Stephens joined the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] for the [[2016 NBA Summer League]]{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/summer-league-roster-160705/|title=Grizzlies announce NBA Summer League 2016 roster|work=NBA.com|date=July 5, 2016|access-date=January 5, 2017}} and on August 8, 2016, he signed with them.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/selden-stephens-williams-wroten-signed-160808|title=Grizzlies sign Wayne Selden Jr., D.J. Stephens, Troy Williams and Tony Wroten|work=NBA.com|date=August 8, 2016|access-date=August 8, 2016}} However, he was waived on October 22 after appearing in five preseason games.{{cite news|url=http://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/sampson-selden-stephens-waived-161022|title=Grizzlies waive JaKarr Sampson, Wayne Selden Jr. & D.J. Stephens|work=NBA.com|date=October 22, 2016|access-date=October 22, 2016}} On November 21, 2016, he signed with Ukrainian club [[BC Budivelnyk|Budivelnyk]] for the rest of the season.{{cite news|title=Будивельник подписал Ди Джея Стивенса!|url=http://budivelnyk.ua/news-ru/946-budivelnik-podpisal-di-dzheya-stivensa|access-date=November 21, 2016|work=budivelnyk.ua|date=November 21, 2016|language=uk|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161122001043/http://budivelnyk.ua/news-ru/946-budivelnik-podpisal-di-dzheya-stivensa|archive-date=November 22, 2016|url-status=dead}} With Budivelnyk he won the [[Ukrainian Basketball SuperLeague|Ukrainian SuperLeague]] championship.{{cite news|title=Budivelnyk wins the 2016/17 Superleague title|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/ukraine/233880/budivelnyk-wins-the-2016-17-superleague-title.html|access-date=May 13, 2017|work=Sportando.com|date=May 6, 2017}} ===Vaqueros de Bayamón (2017)=== On May 19, 2017, Stephens signed with [[Vaqueros de Bayamón]] of the [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional]].{{cite news|title=Stephens será el nuevo refuerzo vaquero|url=http://www.primerahora.com/deportes/baloncesto/nota/stephensseraelnuevorefuerzovaquero-1225184/|access-date=September 14, 2017|work=primerahora.com|date=May 19, 2017|language=Spanish}} ===Le Mans Sarthe Basket (2017–2018)=== On July 17, 2017, Stephens signed with French club [[Le Mans Sarthe Basket]] for the 2017–18 season.{{cite news|title=D.J. Stephens en couteau suisse à l'intérieur|url=http://www.msb.fr/index.php/club/44-informations-generales/3739-d-j-stephens-en-couteau-suisse-a-l-interieur|access-date=September 14, 2017|work=msb.fr|date=July 17, 2017|language=French|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170915071413/http://www.msb.fr/index.php/club/44-informations-generales/3739-d-j-stephens-en-couteau-suisse-a-l-interieur|archive-date=September 15, 2017|url-status=dead}} On May 15, 2018, Stephens was named the [[LNB Pro A Best Sixth Man]] of the 2017–18 season.[http://www.lnb.fr/fr/Accueil/100003/Article/38021/Zach-Peacock-dans-l-histoire Zach Peacock dans l'histoire] He averaged 9.1 points and 3.7 rebounds per game. Stephens to two-way contract |url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/memphis-grizzlies-sign-d-j-stephens-to-two-way-contract-181008|date=October 8, 2018|website=NBA.com|access-date=October 9, 2018}} but was waived by the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] on December 30, 2018, after appearing in one game.{{cite web|title=Memphis Grizzlies waive D.J. Stephens|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/memphis-grizzlies-waive-dj-stephens-181230|date=December 30, 2018|website=NBA.com|access-date=December 30, 2018}} ===Manama Club (2019)=== On February 19, 2019, Stephens signed a contract for the rest of the season with the reigning [[Bahraini Premier League (basketball)|Bahraini Premier League]] champions, [[Manama Club (basketball)|Manama Club]]. He posted averages of 18 ppg, 10 rpg, and 2.7 assist a game. He announced his departure April 13, 2019, via Instagram. ===Le Mans Sarthe Basket (2019–2020)=== On July 12, 2019, he has signed with [[Le Mans Sarthe Basket|Le Mans]] of the [[LNB Pro A]].{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/dj-stephens-returns-to-le-mans/|title=DJ Stephens returns to Le Mans|date=July 12, 2019|newspaper=Sportando|language=En|access-date=August 14, 2019|last1=Carchia |first1=Emiliano }} On December 29, 2019, he has won the dunk contest of the French All-Star Game LNB 2019. He averaged 8.6 points and 3.5 rebounds per game.{{cite news |title=D.J. Stephens joins BC Prometey |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/d-j-stephens-joins-bc-prometey/ |website=Sportando |access-date=July 9, 2020 |date=July 9, 2020|last1=Skerletic |first1=Dario }} ===Prometey (2020–2022)=== On July 9, 2020, Stephens signed with [[BC Prometey|Prometey]] of the [[Ukrainian Basketball SuperLeague]]. He averaged 12 points, 5.4 rebounds, 1.8 assists, and 1.4 steals per game. Stephens re-signed with the team on July 3, 2021.{{cite web |title=Stephens re-signs at Prometey |url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Basketball-Champions-League/news/692206/Stephens-re-signs-at-Prometey |website=Eurobasket |access-date=July 3, 2021 |date=July 3, 2021}} He averaged 12.4 points, 5.0 rebounds, and 1.3 steals per game, helping the team win the Supercup. ===Fos Provence (2022)=== On March 17, 2022, he has signed with [[Fos Provence Basket|Fos Provence]] of the [[LNB Pro A]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Ukraine/news/735627/D.J.-Stephens-(ex-Prometey)-agreed-terms-with-Fos-Provence|title=D.J.
